claims.text: An MLP trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations can improve the representation of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed improvement applies to both solid and liquid alloy states near melting.
The intervention is MLP training using ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
The proposed method is applicable to alloys containing 3–6 principal elements, each at 10–40 at.%.
Short-range and medium-range order in the liquid and solid phases mediate the proposed improvement.
An AIMD-trained MLP improves representation of the relevant atomic configurations.
Improved representation of atomic configurations increases phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
The MLP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 30% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Free-energy differences can be used to measure the claimed reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The applicable temperature range is within 100 K of each alloy's melting point.
MLP transferability across compositions and temperatures is uncertain and may be limited by the training data.
The proposed benchmark compares MLP- and EAM-referenced free-energy calculations against ab initio benchmarks for a set of high-entropy alloys.
The benchmark measures free-energy differences and phase-space-overlap metrics.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if MLP-based free energies deviate from ab initio benchmarks by more than 50 meV/atom.
